thread:
maya: quick FYI — uploaded weights for 'citrine-v2' to gs://redwood-models/citrine/v2 and started a quick smoke deploy. noticed tokenizer differences vs atlas_tokenizer: the chat template uses <|sep|> sentinel but atlas maps it to token id 502, while our runtime tokenizer maps to 25502. this is shifting prompt lengths for a few test prompts. anyone oncall for tokenizer quirks?
liam: on it. can you paste the exact prompt + tokenizer config you used?
sara: tagging infra for the gs path, maya — did you update model metadata with quantization/ft metadata? we need model-card locked before Dedicated pulls it.
maya: here — prompt example 
```
system: "You are Citrine. Answer concisely."
user: "Summarize: a. the change b. potential regression axes <|sep|> test-case-1"
```
and tokenizer config: 
`special_tokens: {sep: "<|sep|>", bos: "<s>", eos: "</s>"}`
liam: ok the mismatch explains off-by-one in token counts. runtime expects sentinel id in 25000+ range for user-defined sentinels; atlas uses reserved 502. two options: remap sentinel to reserved id during onboarding, or update chat template to use bos/eos-only wrapper and avoid that sentinel. both have tradeoffs.
jun: quick check — can we shim mapping at load time? `tokenizer.add_special_tokens({'sep':'<|sep|>'})` then `tokenizer.encoder['<|sep|>']=25502` should work but will require model-card note and test updates. infra-bot: smoke-deploy started for citrine-v2 on host gpu-22 — logs: https://deploys/redwood/citrine-v2/1715123456
sara: @maya can you flip a config and run the unit set? small script below to validate len parity between atlas and runtime: 
```python
# run in repo tools/tokenizer_checks
from tokenizer_utils import atlas_encode, runtime_encode
for p in open('tests/prompt_samples.txt'):
    a=atlas_encode(p)
    r=runtime_encode(p)
    if len(a)!=len(r):
        print('mismatch', p[:40])
```
liam: also pinging @jun for a quick code-review on the onboarding PR — it's tiny: remap special token id if incoming model.json specifies `special_token_override: true`. PR link: https://git/repo/pulls/812
maya: ran the script — 4 mismatches, all due to <|sep|> occurrences. i prefer a shim at load time for backward compat (less customer-facing break).
jun: agree on shim. will review PR tonight. one caveat: need to add a config flag `preserve_reserved_ids: false` default false? or true? maybe default true to preserve reserved when model explicitly set.
liam: let's set default to preserve (true). that way models that intentionally used reserved ids don't break. add a unit test that asserts `token_id('<|sep|>') == model_spec.expected_sep_id`.
maya: updated model metadata with quant=fp16 and added model-card note: 'special_token_override: true -> runtime will remap <|sep|> to high-id range unless preserve_reserved_ids=true'
deploy-bot: deploy citrine-v2 smoke completed on gpu-22 — all health checks passed except tokenizer parity tests (4 failures).
sara: next steps: jun to review + merge PR, liam to add unit tests, maya to rerun onboarding smoke with preserve_reserved_ids=true toggle, infra to promote if green. i'll own the model-card lock and metadata.
maya: thanks all — i'm going to run the rerun now and will drop results here in ~15m. :hourglass:
liam: thx — @jun and @sara if you want i can also add a small compatibility check to the onboarding pipeline that flags models whose special tokens collide with reserved ids. would save this going forward.
jun: yes pls, that check would have saved us last week too. i'll leave a TODO in the PR.
maya: results: rerun with preserve_reserved_ids=true -> parity fixed, all tests pass. pushing model-card final. :tada:
